title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power De Rham complex. Grothendieck is trying to classify, almost tautologically, the possible 'operations' on additive (co)homological invariants of simplicial sets. The previous page proved a universal property: the abelianization functor X ↦ Z(X), from simplicial sets (Δ^) to simplicial abelian groups (Δ^_ab = Fun(Δ^op, Ab) ≃ Ab_*), is the universal colimit-preserving functor into additive cocomplete categories. Equivalently, colimit-preserving functors Ab_* → A correspond to functors Δ → A. In particular the cosimplicial object n ↦ Z[Δ^n] in Ab_* is the universal cosimplicial object in additive categories with colimits, for colimit-preserving functors. He labels this a 'Corollaire (Dold-Puppe)'.

This page:
(a) Passing through the Dold–Kan (Dold–Puppe) correspondence, the associated (co)chain complex in Ab_* is universal for cochain complexes in additive cocomplete A. One may also replace Ab_* by Ab. (chain complexes) in describing the category that holds the universal object.
(b) Dually, C_*(Δ^n), viewed as a simplicial object of (Ab_*)^op = (Ab^op)_* with limits, is universal for categories B with limits and limit-preserving functors. The same holds for the associated chain complex.

Reformulation 'from the viewpoint of universal algebra':
1. Contravariant additive invariants F of X_* ∈ Ss that turn colimits into limits, with values in an additive A, are the same as simplicial objects K_* of A (K_n = F(Δ^n)). Equivalently, via normalization ND and Dold–Puppe DP, they are chain complexes K. of A. The formulas are F(X) ≅ Hom_*(C_*(X), K_*) ≅ Hom.(C.(X), K.), with K. = ND.(K_*) and K_* = DP_*(K.).
2. Natural 'operations' Ω on such invariants, compatible with limit-preserving functors A → A', are given by objects L_* ∈ Ab_* (or L. ∈ Ab.). The formula is Ω(F) ≅ Hom_*(L_*, K_*) ≅ Hom.(L., K.). This is a 2-categorical Yoneda statement: the 'theory' of such invariants is (Ab_*)^op, i.e. the category of simplicial abelian groups.
1'), 2') Dually, covariant invariants commuting with limits(sic) correspond to cosimplicial objects K^* or cochain complexes K^·, with G(X) ≅ C_*(X) ⊗_Δ K^* (a coend) ≅ C.(X) ⊗ K^·. Operations act by Ω(G) ≅ L_* ⊗ K^*.

A margin note says Ω has two variant expressions, on K^* and on K^·. The next page then refines this: restricting the class L of (co)limits that are required gives smaller universal categories, namely the full subcategories of Ab_* generated under L-type colimits. This anticipates the theory of free completion under a class of colimits.
errors: Variance/limit bookkeeping is loose: a contravariant invariant F(X) = Hom(C_*(X), K_*) turns colimits into limits, so A needs limits, not colimits as written in item 1. Grothendieck himself flags the A/B (opposite category) swap on the next page.
In the dual formulas he writes K^* = ND^*(K^·), but the inverse of normalization should be the (co)Dold–Puppe functor DP^*. ND^* appears twice where one should be DP.
The Dold–Kan correspondence in A requires A to be idempotent-complete (Karoubian). This is automatic when A has (co)equalizers, so it is not a real gap.
The meaning of Hom_*, Hom. and ⊗ (ends/coends, i.e. A-valued Hom from an abelian group object to an object of A) is explicitly left 'à expliquer' / 'à préciser'.

ideas.what: Z(Δ^n) cosimplicial simplicial abelian group as the universal cosimplicial object in additive cocomplete categories; colimit-preserving functors sAb → A ≃ Fun(Δ, A)
ideas.modern_name: free additive (Ab-enriched) cocompletion / enriched Kan extension, Yoneda extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958); Kelly (enriched); set-valued version in SGA4 Exp. I
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. I (set-valued version of Hom_!(Ĉ,E) ≃ Hom(C,E)); additive version unsure

ideas.what: Transferring the universal object to chain complexes via normalization / Dold–Puppe in a general additive category
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence for idempotent-complete additive categories

ideas.what: Representing contravariant/covariant additive invariants of simplicial sets as Hom(C_*(X), K_*) or C_*(X) ⊗_Δ K^*
ideas.modern_name: (co)homology with coefficients in a (co)simplicial object; end/coend (weighted limit/colimit) formulas

ideas.what: Natural operations on such invariants (compatible with all (co)limit-preserving functors between value categories) are classified by objects of sAb (resp. chain complexes): Ω(F) = Hom(L_*, K_*)
ideas.modern_name: 2-categorical Yoneda / Lawvere-style 'structure–semantics': the doctrine of additive invariants has theory (sAb)^op
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lawvere (functorial semantics); Kelly–Street (2-categorical Yoneda); not usually stated in this form

ideas.what: (next page) Restricting the class L of required (co)limits yields smaller universal categories: the full subcategory of sAb generated by L-colimits
ideas.modern_name: free completion under a class of colimits / closure of a class of colimits
ideas.usually_credited_to: Albert–Kelly (1988), Kelly 'Basic concepts of enriched category theory' (1982)
ideas.where_published: possibly echoed in Pursuing Stacks discussions of 'modelizers' and universal properties; unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck frames the classification of operations on additive (co)homological invariants of simplicial sets as a universal-algebra / doctrine problem. Operations = objects of Ab_* (opposite), via a 2-categorical Yoneda argument. Refining by the class of admitted (co)limits gives smaller 'theories', anticipating Albert–Kelly's closure of a class of colimits. In the context of the divided-power De Rham talk, the evident aim is to explain where structures such as divided powers / Dold–Puppe derived functors come from. That is an unusual motivation for this formalism.
missed.quote: Du point de vue de l'algèbre universelle, ... réflexions de la façon suivante ... Les constructions qu'on peut faire sur de tels invariants ... s'expriment à l'aide des objets de (Ab_*)°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean 1-categorical precursor of the ∞-categorical statement that natural operations on (co)homology theories are corepresented by the universal object (e.g. spectra / endomorphisms of the sphere). It is also a template for classifying operations on non-additive (e.g. divided-power) invariants. It is mostly folklore today, so the novelty is modest.

missed.claim: Meanings of Hom_*, Hom. and the tensor products are left undefined, and the 'principes généraux' behind the restricted-limit-class statement are explicitly not detailed.
missed.quote: à préciser la signification de ces formules
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a record of intent; the general principles are now standard enriched category theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard: free additive cocompletion, Dold–Kan, coend formulas. The universal-algebra reading of 'operations on invariants' as objects of sAb, with a graded refinement by classes of colimits, is a nice and somewhat early formulation in Grothendieck's hand, but specialists would recognize it as folklore or later Kelly-school theory.
transcription_corrections: Item 1 should read roughly: 's'expriment en termes d'objet simplicial ou dual(ement) en termes de complexes de chaînes de A' (the duplicated 'de A' is an artifact).
Margin note (center): 'Ω a deux expressions variantes, comme opérations sur des K* (Ω*) et opér. sur des K· (Ω·) — qui se traduisent par des objets de B ...' (partly illegible).
Margin note near G formulas: 'à préciser la signification de ces formules' — placed beside the covariant formulas, not inline.
In the G formulas, the crossed-out symbols before ⊗ should be ignored; read G(X_*) ≃ C_*(X_*) ⊗^* K^* ≃ C.(X_*) ⊗^· K^·.
